title: Full faithfulness of lisse restriction on a parameter-root limit
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a characteristic-$p$ field $k$ and a finite norm-topological extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Put $C_E(P)=C(P,E)$ for all profinite sets $P$ using all continuous maps, and use its pulled-back coefficient rings and internal modules [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Let $Y$ be a regular separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $B\to Y$ an affine etale chart, and $V(t_1\cdots t_r)$ a reduced strict normal crossings divisor whose branches on $B$ are precisely $V(t_d)$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary]. For an affine pro-etale $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to B$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], set
$$T=\operatorname{Spec}\left(\varinjlim_{(n,p)=1}R[x_{d,n}]_{1\le d\le r}/(x_{d,n}^n-t_d)_d\right),\qquad T^\circ=T\times_B B[1/(t_1\cdots t_r)].$$
The index is positive integers prime to $p$ ordered by divisibility, with $x_{d,n}\mapsto x_{d,m}^{m/n}$ for $n\mid m$. A lisse module means pro-etale locally finite free over the pulled-back $C_E$ [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. If $j:T^\circ\hookrightarrow T$ is the open inclusion, then for all finite-rank lisse $C_{E,T}$-modules $\mathcal N,\mathcal N'$ the restriction map
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{C_{E,T}}(\mathcal N,\mathcal N')\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{C_{E,T^\circ}}(j^*\mathcal N,j^*\mathcal N')$$
is a bijection. These bijections commute with pro-etale base change of $U$. They include the empty parameter list, rank zero, and the empty chart. No assertion about extending objects from $T^\circ$ is made.

proof.text: Write $T=\operatorname{Spec}S$ and $s=t_1\cdots t_r$. For each affine pro-etale object $W=\operatorname{Spec}Q\to T$, the site definition gives a weakly etale $S$-algebra $Q$. The root presentation and the hypotheses on $Y,B,R$ are exactly those of [lem-sfb-snc-root-limit-normal-charts]; hence $Q$ is normal and multiplication by $s$ is injective. The localization universal property identifies $W^\circ=W\times_TT^\circ$ with $\operatorname{Spec}Q[1/s]$.

proof.text: The norm on $E$ is nonarchimedean. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-principal-open-continuous-sections] to each pair $(Q,s)$ from step 1 and to the affine site object $W\to T$. It gives the actual ring bijection $\Gamma(W,C_{E,T})\to\Gamma(W^\circ,C_{E,T^\circ})$, naturally on affine charts. Thus the coefficient-section hypothesis of the lisse Hom descent lemma holds on the entire affine basis.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-sectionwise-open-lisse-hom-descent] to $j:T^\circ\hookrightarrow T$, $\Lambda=C_E$ and the given lisse modules $\mathcal N,\mathcal N\prime$. The section hypothesis is step 2, so its Hom bijection is precisely the restriction in the statement. Its matrix characterization and descent include rank zero and the empty chart.

proof.text: For pro-etale $U\prime\to U$, the root presentation base changes to the one over $U\prime$: tensoring takes each generator and relation to its base change and preserves the filtered colimit by its universal property. On affine opens of $U\prime$, steps 1–2 give the coefficient-section bijections. For any affine object over the base-changed tower, refine its inverse images of these opens by affines. Unique local extensions of coefficient sections agree on overlap refinements and glue by the sheaf axiom. This verifies the section hypothesis globally. Coefficients identify by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], and pulled-back free bases witness lisseness. The base-change clause of [lem-sfb-sectionwise-open-lisse-hom-descent] gives both the new Hom bijection and equality of pullback of the extension with extension of the pullback under $j\prime{}^*f^*\cong g^*j^*$. If $r=0$, $s=1$ and $j$ is the identity. Empty charts have singleton Hom sets. Only supplied modules' morphisms were extended.
